lines.text: This is your self-monitoring sheet. It helps you notice how you are doing during the day, and it shows what you are working for.
Across the top are your goals. Each goal says what to do, in your own words, with a picture to help you remember it.
Down the side is your day, one row for each part of it. You check yourself at the end of each part.
Down the side are your checks. When the timer gives you the signal, stop for a moment and check yourself. Then go right back to work.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? Circle the thumbs up if you did, or the thumbs down if you did not.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? Circle the smile if you did, or the frown if you did not.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how did I do? Circle the smile if you did it the whole time, the straight face if you did it some of the time, or the frown if not yet.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? Circle the plus if you did, or the minus if you did not.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? Circle the check mark if you did, or the X if you did not.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? Circle yes if you did, or no if you did not.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how did I do? Circle two if you did it, one if you needed a reminder, or zero if not yet.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how well did I do? Circle a number from one to five. Five means you did it really well.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how did I do? Color in the stars you earned: three stars for your very best, fewer when it was harder.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how did I do? Circle green if you did it, yellow if you did part of it, or red if not yet.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: how did I do? Circle the choice that shows it. The key at the top tells you what each one means.
When a part of the day ends, ask yourself: did I do it? If you did, put a check in the box.
When a part of the day ends, look at the levels at the top of your sheet, and circle the level that matches how you did.
At each signal, ask yourself: was I working? Circle your answer, and get straight back to your work.
Be honest. This sheet is about noticing, not about being perfect.
Your teacher rates you too, without looking at your sheet first. Then the two of you compare.
When your answer matches your teacher's answer, you earn points, even when the answer is no. Telling the truth always pays.
Your teacher's rating gives you your points, and when your rating is the same as your teacher's, you earn a bonus point too.
Your teacher fills in your points for each part of the day, and initials it. At the end of the day, you look at them together.
At the end of the day, count your points and write the total at the bottom of your sheet.
Your goal is at the top. When your points reach your goal, you earn your reward.
There is also a midday check. Reach it by lunch, and you earn a little something extra, right then.
Here is your reward store. Each reward shows how many points it costs. Before the day starts, choose what you are working for, and put it in the box at the top.
Before the day starts, choose what you are working for, from your reward menu. Then you know what your points are for.
Points you do not spend can go in your bank, so you can save up for something bigger.
Your contract is a promise you and your teacher make together. It says what you will do, and what you will earn. You both sign it.

This is your Match the model sheet. At the top is the job. Next to it are pictures of how the job can look when it is done: not yet, almost, and like the model. The number on each picture is the points it is worth.
When you finish the job, look at your work, then look at the pictures. Which one is your work most like? Circle that number in the first column.
Then your teacher looks at your work too, on their own, and circles a number in the second column.

If you both circled the same picture, that is a match. You earn that picture's points plus the bonus, and the best reward. An honest not yet that matches still earns the bonus, so tell the truth about your work.
Before the first real day, practice: look at pictures of other work and pick the model each one is most like. When you get nine out of ten right, you are ready to rate your own.
At first your teacher checks every time. When your ratings match often, the checks come less often, and your own rating counts on the other days.
For the adults: rate on your own before you look at the student's sheet. Praise honest ratings, even an honest no. Never take points away, and give the reward the way it was promised.
Notice, rate, be honest, and count. Every day you practice, it gets a little easier. You can do this!
